```{r}
#| label: load
#| include: false

#dependencies
library(tidyverse)
library(scales, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(systemfonts, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(patchwork)
library(ggtext)
library(ggrepel)
library(waffle)
library(gt, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
library(gtExtras)

#add colors
source("Scripts/98_color_system.R")

# Register the OTF font used for pictograms
fa_path <- "assets/FontAwesome7Free-Solid-900.otf"

#if it doesn't exist, download it
if (!file.exists(fa_path)) {
  dir.create(dirname(fa_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  download.file(
    url      = "https://github.com/FortAwesome/Font-Awesome/raw/6.x/otfs/Font%20Awesome%206%20Free-Solid-900.otf",
    destfile = fa_path,
    mode     = "wb"
  )
}

register_font(
  name  = "FontAwesome7Solid",
  plain = fa_path
)

#load each dataset needed for each tab, stored in a list element
files <- list.files("Dataout", ".rds") |> str_remove(".rds")
walk(
  files,
  ~ assign(.x, read_rds(paste0("Dataout/", .x, ".rds")), envir = .GlobalEnv)
)
```

#### Row {height="40%"}
```{r}
#| label: share-gdp
#| title: "NHE share of GDP"
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Waffle chart with a 10-by-10 grid representing U.S. gross domestic
#|   product in CY 2024. Eighteen of the 100 squares are filled to show that
#|   national health expenditures accounted for 18 percent of GDP.

v_nhe_share <- health_spending[["df_nhe_gdp_share"]] |>
  filter(category == "National Health Expenditures") |>
  pull(value_fmt)

health_spending[["df_nhe_gdp_share"]] |>
  ggplot(aes(fill = fill_color, values = value * 100)) +
  geom_waffle(
    n_rows  = 10,       # 10x10 grid = 100 squares
    size    = 1,      # border between squares
    colour  = "white",  # border colour
    flip    = TRUE      # fill column-by-column (bottom to top)
  ) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  labs(title = v_nhe_share) +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_void(base_family = "Source Sans 3", base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title =
      element_text(
        size = 80, hjust = .5,
        family = "Source Sans 3", face = "bold",
        color = ff_colors$scales$steel["900"]
      ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 24, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40"),
    plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )


```

```{r}
#| label: per_capita
#| title: "NHE per capita"
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Area chart of national health expenditures per person by year.
#|   Per-capita spending rises each year, from $11,582 in CY 2019 to $15,474 in
#|   CY 2024, an increase of about one-third over the period.
#| out-width: 100%
#| out-height: 100%
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 8

health_spending[["df_nhe_pc"]] |> 
  ggplot(aes(data_year, value, fill = fill_color, color = fill_color)) +
  geom_blank(aes(y = value * 1.1)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = ff_colors$elements[["axis"]]) +
  geom_area(alpha = .2) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(y = val_pt), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = lab_val),
    vjust = -1, hjust = .5, na.rm = TRUE,
    family = "Source Sans 3", #size = 8,
    color = ff_colors$elements[["annotation"]]
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks =
      range(
        unique(health_spending[["df_nhe_pc"]]$data_year),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.1))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(.001, .001)) +
  scale_fill_identity() + 
  scale_color_identity() + 
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Source Sans 3", base_size = 50) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text =
      element_markdown(
        color = ff_colors$elements[["title"]],
        face = "bold",
        hjust = 0
      ),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(5, "lines")
  )

```

#### Row

```{r}
#| label: nhe_sources
#| title: "NHE by Source of Funds"
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Horizontal bar chart of CY 2024 national health expenditures by source of
#|   funds. Health insurance is by far the largest source at $3.9 trillion;
#|   out-of-pocket spending is $557 billion, other third-party payers and
#|   programs $433 billion, investment $239 billion, and government public
#|   health activities $158 billion.
#| out-width: 100%
#| out-height: 100%
#| fig-width: 24
#| fig-height: 10

health_spending[["df_nhe_sources"]] |> 
  ggplot(aes(value, fct_reorder(sub_category, value), fill = fill_color)) +
  geom_blank(aes(value * 1.2)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = value_format),
    hjust = -.1,
    family = "Source Sans 3",
    size = 18,
    color = ff_colors$elements[["annotation"]]
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(.001, .001)) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 50,
    base_family = "Source Sans 3",
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 45),
    strip.text =
      element_text(
        family = "Source Sans 3 SemiBold",
        color = ff_colors$scales$steel[["900"]],
        size = 50,
        hjust = 0
      )
  )

```

### Column

```{r}
#| label: insurance_bar
#| title: "National Health Insurance Expenditures by Payer"
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Faceted horizontal bar chart of CY 2024 national health insurance
#|   expenditures by payer. Private health insurance is largest at $1.6
#|   trillion, followed by Medicare at $1.1 trillion and Medicaid at $932
#|   billion; Veterans Affairs, Defense, and CHIP are much smaller at $118
#|   billion, $50 billion, and $31 billion, respectively.
#| fig-height: 8
#| out.height: "100%"
#| fig-width: 9

health_spending[["df_insurance"]] |>
  ggplot(aes(value, fct_reorder(sub_category, value), fill = fill_color)) +
  geom_blank(aes(value * 1.3)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = value_fmt),
    hjust = -.2, size = 8,
    family = "Source Sans 3",
    color = ff_colors$elements[["annotation"]]
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~fct_reorder(sub_category, value, .desc = TRUE),
    ncol = 1, scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(.005, .005)) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    strip.text =
      element_text(
        family = "Source Sans 3 SemiBold",
        color = ff_colors$scales$steel[["900"]],
        size = 25, hjust = 0
      ),
    panel.spacing = unit(0, "lines"),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fed_spend_pictogram
#| title: "CMS Spending by Category"
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Faceted horizontal bar chart of CMS spending by category. Of $1.9
#|   trillion in federal program spending, Medicare benefits account for
#|   $1.158 trillion, or 61 percent, and Medicaid for $687 billion, or 36
#|   percent; CHIP and other spending are about 1 percent each. Separate
#|   panels divide $8 billion in program management between a $4.1 billion
#|   appropriation and $3.4 billion from other sources, and show $2.6 billion
#|   for health care fraud and abuse control. Data are from CY 2024.
#| out-width: 100%
#| out-height: 100%
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8

health_spending[["df_spend"]] |>
  ggplot(aes(value, sub_category, fill = fill_color)) +
  geom_blank(aes(value * 1.2)) +
  geom_col(width = .8) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = value_fmt),
    family = "Source Sans 3",
    color = ff_colors$elements[["annotation"]],
    hjust = -.1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~fct_rev(category), ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y", space = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(.005, .005)) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 28,
    base_family = "Source Sans 3",
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 28),
    strip.text =
      element_text(
        family = "Source Sans 3 SemiBold",
        color = ff_colors$scales$steel[["900"]],
        size = 28,
        hjust = 0
      )
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fte
#| title: "CMS Full-Time Equivalents (FTEs)"
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Pictogram of six person symbols representing the approximate scale of
#|   CMS staffing, one person symbol per 1,000 staff. The prominently displayed

)

icons |>

  geom_text(
    label  = "\uf007",              # Font Awesome "person" / user icon

    size   = 50,

  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  labs(title    = health_spending$fte[["value_fmt"]]) +
  theme_void(base_family = "Source Sans 3") +
  theme(
    plot.title =
      element_text(
        size = 80,
        hjust = .5,
        face = "bold",
        color = ff_colors$scales$steel["900"]
      ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 30, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40"),
    plot.caption  = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray60"),
    plot.margin   = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )

```

#### Row {height="65%"}

```{r}
#| label: medicare_trend
#| title: >-
#|   Medicare Advantage Now Exceeds
#|    Original Medicare Beneficiaries
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Two-line chart of Medicare beneficiaries by program from CY 2008 through
#|   2025. Medicare Advantage enrollment climbs from 10 million, or 22
#|   percent, to 35.3 million, or 51 percent, while Original Medicare moves
#|   from 35.5 million, or 78 percent, to 34.0 million, or 49 percent. The
#|   lines cross in CY 2024; dotted final segments indicate preliminary
#|   CY 2025 values.
#| out-width: 100%
#| out-height: 100%
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 8

medicare[["df_medicare_trend"]]  |> 
  ggplot(aes(data_year, value, group = sub_category, fill = fill_color, color = fill_color)) +
  geom_blank(aes(y = value * 1.1)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = medicare[["df_medicare_ribbon"]],
    aes(x = data_year, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    fill = ff_colors$base["warmgray"], alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linetype = 'dotted',
    linewidth = 2.5
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = medicare[["df_medicare_trend"]]  |> filter(data_year != 2025),
    linewidth = 3
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(y = lab_pos, label = end_labs),  
    color = ff_colors$elements[["annotation"]],
    hjust = .1, na.rm = TRUE,
    family = "Source Sans 3"
  ) + 
  geom_label(
    aes(y = lab_cat_pos, label = lab_cat), 
    color = "white",
    na.rm = TRUE, hjust = .3,
    family = "Source Sans 3 SemiBold"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(y = end_pt), na.rm = TRUE,
    shape = 21, size = 8, color = "white",
    stroke = 5 
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    label = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale()),
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = c(.001, .001)
    ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(
      min(medicare[["df_medicare_trend"]]$data_year),
      max(medicare[["df_medicare_trend"]]$data_year) + 3
    ),
    breaks = seq(
      from = min(medicare[["df_medicare_trend"]]$data_year),
      to = max(medicare[["df_medicare_trend"]]$data_year),
      by = 1
    ),
    labels = medicare[["trend_year_labels"]]
  ) +
  scale_color_identity(aesthetics = c("color", "fill")) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + 
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL, 
    caption = str_glue('Note: CY {max(medicare[["df_medicare_trend"]]$data_year)} values are preliminary')
    ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Source Sans 3", base_size = 30)  +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 24, color = "#909090"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "gray80")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: medicare_disagg_trend
#| title: "Medicare Sub-Populations Trends"
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Faceted area chart with one panel each for aged and disabled
#|   Medicare beneficiaries from CY 2008 through 2025. The aged population
#|   increases steadily from 38 million to 62 million, while the disabled
#|   population rises to nearly 9 million in the mid-2010s and then declines
#|   to about 7 million. The CY 2025 endpoints are preliminary.
#| out-width: 100%
#| out-height: 100%
#| fig-width: 24
#| fig-height: 8

medicare[["df_medicare_disagg_trend"]] |> 
  ggplot(
    aes(
      data_year, value,
      group = sub_category,
      fill = fill_color, color = fill_color
    )
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = ff_colors$elements[["axis"]]) +
  geom_area(alpha = .4) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(aes(y = val_pt), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = lab_val),
    vjust = -1, na.rm = TRUE,
    family = "Source Sans 3", size = 20,
    color = ff_colors$elements[["annotation"]]
  ) +
  facet_grid(. ~ fct_reorder2(sub_category, data_year, value), switch = "y") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = range(medicare[["df_medicare_disagg_trend"]]$data_year),
    minor_breaks = 
      seq(
        min(medicare[["df_medicare_disagg_trend"]]$data_year), 
        max(medicare[["df_medicare_disagg_trend"]]$data_year)
      ),

  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(.001, .001)) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +

    caption = str_glue('Note: CY {max(medicare[["df_medicare_disagg_trend"]]$data_year)} values are preliminary')

    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text =
      element_text(
        color = ff_colors$elements[["title"]],
        face = "bold"
      ),
    strip.placement = "outside",

    plot.caption = element_text(size = 50, color = "#909090"),

    # axis.minor.ticks.x.bottom = element_line(color = "gray60"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing = unit(6, "lines")
  )
```

#### Row

```{r}
#| label: orig_medicare_utilization
#| title: Original Medicare Utilization & Spending
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Scatter chart of six Original Medicare service types, with persons
#|   served on the horizontal axis and program payments on the vertical axis.
#|   Physician and durable medical equipment services reach the most people,
#|   28.4 million, and have the highest payments, $132.7 billion; inpatient
#|   hospital services have nearly the same payments, $131.2 billion, but
#|   serve 4.8 million people. Other service types serve fewer people and
#|   account for lower payments.
#| out-width: 100%
#| out-height: 100%
#| fig-width: 22
#| fig-height: 22

medicare[["df_medicare_util"]] |>
  ggplot(aes(persons_served, payments, fill = category)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = category), color = "white", size = 20, alpha = 1) +
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = sub_category),
    point.padding = 30,
    box.padding = 1,
    force_pull = 0.3,
    force = 20,
    min.segment.length = 0,
    family = "Source Sans 3",
    color = ff_colors$elements[["annotation"]],
    size = 18
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      ff_colors$scales$cobolt[["300"]],
      ff_colors$scales$cobolt[["700"]],
      ff_colors$scales$cobolt[["500"]]
    )
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 23, 22)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(prefix = "$", scale_cut = cut_short_scale()),
    limits = c(0, NA),
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Persons Served", y = "Program Payments", 
    caption = medicare[["v_hha_caption"]],
    fill = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 60, base_family = "Source Sans 3") +
  theme(
    panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines"),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 45),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = ff_colors$scales$warmgray["100"], color = ff_colors$scales$warmgray["100"]),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 45, color = "#909090"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

##### Column

```{r}
#| label: part_d_util
#| title: Part D Utilization
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Two-panel line chart of Medicare Part D utilization from CY 2019 through
#|   2024. Utilizing beneficiaries increase steadily from 45.1 million to
#|   53.3 million, while prescription drug events remain near 1.5 billion
#|   through 2022 before increasing to 1.7 billion in 2024.
#| out-width: 100%
#| out-height: 100%
#| fig-width: 26
#| fig-height: 8

medicare[["df_part_d_util"]] |>
  ggplot(aes(x = data_year, y = value, group = sub_category)) +
  geom_blank(aes(y = value * 1.2)) +
  geom_blank(aes(y = value * .8)) +
  geom_line(color = ff_colors$scales$cobolt[["700"]], linewidth = 3.5) +
  geom_point(
    aes(y = end_point), na.rm = TRUE, 
    color = ff_colors$scales$cobolt[["700"]], size = 10
    ) +
  geom_text(aes(label = point_value_lab, hjust = lab_offset), size = 20, na.rm = TRUE) + 
  facet_grid(sub_category ~ .,  scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  labs(
    x    = NULL, 
    y    = NULL,
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(
      min(medicare[["df_part_d_util"]]$data_year) - 2, 
      max(medicare[["df_part_d_util"]]$data_year) + 2
      ),
    expand = c(0, 0),
    breaks = range(medicare[["df_part_d_util"]]$data_year) #NULL
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(.001, .001), breaks = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Source Sans 3", base_size = 50) +
  theme(
```

```{r}
    hjust = -.1, family = "Source Sans 3",
    color = ff_colors$elements[["annotation"]],
    size = 14
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(.005, .005)) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 45) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title =
      element_text(
        face = "bold",
        color = ff_colors$elements[["title"]]
      )
  )
```

# Notes

## Row 

### Column

::: {.card}

# Health Spending 

  - Total Medicaid Amount reported as total gross outlays including the Vaccines for Children Program.

# Medicare Enrollment/Utilization
  
  - Populations may not add due to rounding
  - Medicare Advantage (MA) total includes both MA and other health plan enrollment
  - Medicare CY2025 and Medicaid & CHIP  data points are preliminary and subject to change 

# Medicare Cost Sharing

  - The inpatient hospital deductible applies per benefit period.  
  - For Part D, the initial coverage limit was eliminated in 2025. More information can be found [here](https://www.cms.gov/files/document/final-cy-2025-part-d-redesign-program-instructions.pdf)
  
# Medicare Providers

  - In historic Fast Facts files, Labs are categorized as Institutional Providers, but can in fact call under any category. As such, they have been seperated out here so as not to add into the total for Institutional Providers.
  - Non-Institutional Proviers - Providers utilized by Original Medicare beneficiaries for all Part B non-institutional/DMEPOS provider services.  Providers may be counted in more than one specialty classification but are reported as a single provider in the "Total Providers" count.
:::

### Column

::: {.card}

# Medicaid Enrollment/Utilization

  - Populations may not add due to rounding
  - Total count represent the number of Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries with comprehensive coverage.  The categories are sourced from data that include beneficiaries with non-comprehensive coverage and do not sum to the total counts.
  - Dual Eligible includes Aged, Disabled & ESRD; Counts represent full-benefit eligible individuals.
  - 2025 data not yet available for Dual Eligible and Medicaid Expansion Adults
  - Payments for All Services includes payments for additional services not broken out separately.
  - Fee-for-service payments = (a) Inpatient Services, (b) Long-Term Care, (c) Physician, Laboratory, and Other Services, and (d) Prescription Drugs
  - Expenditures by service category do not sum to the total expenditures.  Total expenditures also include Medicare payments for some beneficiaries and adjustments to prior year payments.  Managed care expenditures cover the same services that are delivered via fee-for-service.  Data do not permit allocation of managed care expenditures to the different service categories.  These expenditures are from all Medicaid beneficiaries, regardless of eligibility. 
  - The Medicaid & CHIP population and expenditure data are from the [Medicaid & CHIP scorecard](https://www.medicaid.gov/state-overviews/scorecard/who-enrolls-medicaid-chip/index.html)


# Abbreviations

  - CHIP - Children's Health Insurance Program
  - DMEPOS - Medicare Durable Medical Equipment, Prosthetics, Orthotics and Supplies
  - LTR - Life Time Reserve
  - MA - Medicare Advantage
  - MAPD - Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug Plan
  - PDP - Prescription Drug Plan
  - PT - Physical Therapy
  - SNF - Skilled Nursing Facility

:::
